one_month_reasoning: No AppLovin earnings fall inside 2026-10-02 to 2026-10-31. Third-party calendars put Q3 2026 at ~Nov 4 (unconfirmed; no 8-K or date release on EDGAR as of Oct 2, and last quarter the date was announced Jul 1 for an Aug 5 report, so an early-October date release is likely and carries no information). The Nov 16 lead-plaintiff deadline is also outside the window. Inside it: the FOMC (Oct 27-28), Meta/Alphabet Q3 prints in late October (read-across on ad demand and AI ad tooling), and more sell-side alt-data notes; Wells Fargo's Sep 30 pixel note and Edgewater's Sep 23 note each moved the stock ~4.5-5% in a day, and a July BofA note moved it 13%. These cut both ways from a 52-week low, where short-term reversal and negative momentum roughly cancel. The Q3 guide already includes the post-quarter model step-up (CFO: it 'reflects the model improvements that are already live'), so there is no in-window event that tests it. I therefore use a symmetric lognormal centred on spot ($281) with monthly sigma 21% (75%/3.5) and no directional call.

fair_value.method: Blend of 50% P/E (NTM EPS at Oct-2027 ~$21.8 x 16x = $349) and 50% FCF yield (NTM FCF ~$6.8B at a 6% yield on ~326M shares = $348). FY27 EPS is consensus $20.00 cut 4% to $19.2; net debt (~$0.46B) is immaterial.

bear.story: Gaming growth flattens (Edgewater's MAX 'functional ceiling', Unity Vector spread pressure) and model gains stay lumpy. E-commerce stays a 'false start' on traffic-weighted data because generative video creative (management's 'biggest hurdle') slips further. FY27 EPS lands ~$16 and the stock de-rates to ~10.5x NTM EPS of ~$16.5.

base.story: Q4 grows ~8-10% q/q, 2027 revenue grows ~22-27% with EBITDA margin ~82-83%. FY27 EPS ~$19-19.5, buybacks ~$3B+/yr. E-commerce starts contributing in H2 2027. The multiple recovers only partly, to ~15x an NTM EPS of ~$21.5.

bull.story: The post-Q2 model step-up keeps compounding, Q3/Q4 beat the guide, and traffic-weighted e-commerce adoption turns in early 2027 once video creative ships. FY27 EPS ~$22 and the stock re-rates to ~18x NTM EPS of ~$27 as revisions turn up.

thesis_break_reason: $180 is ~9.4x my FY27 EPS ($19.2), 9x consensus ($20.00) and a ~10% FCF yield for a business with ~83% EBITDA margins, near-zero capex and ~$0.46B net debt. There the market would be pricing an earnings decline, not slower growth: a Q4 guide implying flat or negative q/q revenue, sequential declines from Axon model degradation or share loss to Unity/Meta, an Apple/Google platform policy shock, or a damaging litigation disclosure (the SEC inquiry is closed, so the remaining legal risk is the two class actions). It is about one 12-month sigma below spot, so a sustained trade there needs fundamental confirmation, which I would treat as the break.

reasoning: Round 2. Primary documents still show a fast-compounding business: Q2 2026 revenue $1.924B (+53%), 83.9% adj. EBITDA margin, $3.76 GAAP EPS, Q3 guide $2.055-2.085B (+46-48%), net debt ~$0.46B, $1.8B buyback authorisation left. Corrections from the supervisor, which I verified: (1) the Q3 guide is not conservative in the way I said; the CFO said it 'reflects the model improvements that are already live and performing' (the step-up that landed just after quarter-end) and excludes only not-yet-deployed releases; (2) Edgewater's Q4 call (+8-9% q/q) is only ~1-2% below consensus; (3) Wells Fargo's traffic-weighted pixel data pushes e-commerce to 2027. Re-reading the call I also found I overstated the buyback pace: Q2 repurchases were $551M, moderated from ~$1B in Q1. I therefore cut FY27 EPS 4% to $19.2, FY28 growth to 18%, the P/E to 16x and the share-count reduction, which lowers fair value from $382 to $348 (P/E $349, FCF yield $348). I remain above the supervisor's ~$320 because 15x NTM is roughly today's de-rated multiple and assumes no re-rating at all for a business still guiding ~46% growth; a modest move to 16x is a judgment I keep. The scenario mix (30% bear $175, 45% base $320, 25% bull $490) gives a mean of ~$319. I do not centre the distribution on fair value because revisions are falling and momentum is negative. The ladder is a mixture: 92% lognormal with median $308 and sigma 0.55, plus 8% business-break mass with median $155. That gives P(>=281) 0.53, slightly below round 1's 0.545, and a thinner right tail (P>=703 0.062 vs 0.071). EDGAR shows no new 8-K since Aug 5. Research was mostly SEC filings and the call transcript; consensus is from Alpha Vantage, and option data was deliberately not consulted.
